newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL interbank rates firm despite Negara lending.
newsitem.headline: KL interbank rates firm despite Negara lending.

text.p: Interbank rates remained firm on Monday despite further injection of funds by the central Bank Negara Malaysia, dealers said.
"Negara is again lending one-month money at 8.5 percent. There are a lot of bids out there," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
He said despite the central bank lending, rates held firm as the market was too short.
Dealers said the current squeeze was caused by some month-end ringgit demand.
One-month money was steady at 8.50 percent while three-month was also unchanged at 8.30 percent.
Bank Negara is said to have injected funds over the past two weeks to help ease market tightness.
Recent heavy buying of the ringgit by the central bank to defend the currency from speculative attack had caused a liquidity squeeze.
There was no confirmation of the funds injection from Bank Negara, which does not usually comment on its market operations.
Dealers said maturity of Bank Negara bills worth 500 million ringgit on Friday was unlikely to have much impact on interbank rates.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange rebounded after recent falls.
At 0330 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was up six points to 92.30, or an implied yield of 7.70 percent.
The December contract rose four to 92.53, or 7.47 percent while March 1998 was up five to 92.63, or 7.37 percent.
